algorithm.Title: Cough - Chronic - Male (Child)
algorithm.ContentSet: IST Open-Source Guideline Content | Child | Male
Definition: Chronic/persistent cough (3+ weeks) assessment decomposed from NHS.UK's published cough guidance.
FirstAid: Call Qatar 999 now, keep the patient in the easiest breathing position, and do not allow self-driving. For suspected choking, follow the call-handler's age-appropriate first-aid instructions; do not perform a blind finger sweep. Call Qatar 999 now, follow the call-taker's ambulance and emergency-transport instructions, and do not self-drive. Do not delay emergency care.

questions.Question: Is there major coughing of blood, breathing difficulty, blue or grey colour, collapse, confusion, or crushing chest pain?
questions.Information: Major haemoptysis or cardiopulmonary compromise remains a direct Qatar 999 emergency and must not redirect a young child into the age-12-and-older Coughing Up Blood protocol.

questions.Question: Without an emergency feature, is any blood present in the sputum?
questions.Information: Any haemoptysis requires governed prompt in-person assessment. This direct disposition preserves support for children younger than 12 without a permissive age-incompatible redirect.

questions.Question: Is there severe breathing difficulty, blue/grey colour, collapse, confusion, inability to speak or drink, major coughing of blood, crushing chest pain, stridor, or sudden cough after choking or suspected inhaled foreign body, especially in a child?
questions.Information: Airway obstruction, respiratory failure, major haemoptysis, and serious cardiopulmonary symptoms require immediate emergency assessment.

questions.Question: Without an emergency feature, is the cough rapidly worsening, is the person very unwell, or is there breathlessness, chest pain, any blood in sputum, high fever, dehydration, immune suppression, pregnancy, an infant or young child, or tuberculosis exposure or concern?
questions.Information: NHS.UK cough guidance lists these as reasons to seek urgent clinical review immediately.

questions.Question: Has the cough lasted 3 weeks or more, or is it recurrent or associated with unexplained weight loss, night sweats, persistent hoarseness, a neck lump, smoking or vaping, occupational exposure, or a medicine that may cause cough?
questions.Information: NHS.UK guidance recommends routine primary-care review for a cough persisting beyond 3 weeks, or with weight loss or immune compromise.

questions.Question: Is this a mild cough under 3 weeks in an otherwise well older child or adult, with normal breathing and intake and none of the features or higher-risk states above?
questions.Information: NHS.UK guidance describes most coughs under 3 weeks as manageable at home.

advice.Title: Emergency cough and breathing precautions
Content: Call Qatar 999 now, keep the patient in the easiest breathing position, and do not allow self-driving. For suspected choking, follow the call-handler's age-appropriate first-aid instructions; do not perform a blind finger sweep. Call Qatar 999 now, follow the call-taker's ambulance and emergency-transport instructions, and do not self-drive. Do not delay emergency care.
Call Back If: worsening breathing, blue/grey colour, collapse, or reduced responsiveness.

advice.Title: Prompt in-person cough review
Content: Use the Qatar governance-approved in-person service and timeframe. Mention immune suppression, pregnancy, child age, blood, tuberculosis exposure, travel, and breathing symptoms before arrival so infection-control precautions can be arranged.
Call Back If: worsening breathing difficulty, chest pain, increasing blood, confusion, or poor intake.

advice.Title: Persistent-cough investigation
Content: Use the governance-approved Qatar primary-care or respiratory pathway for examination and investigation. Do not stop a prescribed medicine such as an ACE inhibitor without the prescriber's advice, and do not assume a persistent cough is benign.
Call Back If: blood, weight loss, night sweats, chest pain, fever, or breathing difficulty.

advice.Title: Low-risk cough care
Content: Rest, take normal fluids, avoid smoke and vaping, and use honey only for patients aged 1 year or older. Confirm all medicines with a pharmacist for age, pregnancy, chronic disease, interactions, and doses already taken.
Call Back If: cough reaches 3 weeks or becomes recurrent; blood, weight loss, fever, chest pain, poor intake, or breathing difficulty.
